thread:
sam: Customer (AcmeCorp) opened a ticket saying they got repeated 429s from /v1/generate this morning even though the project quota UI shows ~60% used. I'm dropping logs below.
alex: Can you paste the 429 response headers and which project/org IDs they hit?
sam: curl output from their repro:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 15:22:11 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 161
x-request-id: req_01F...
{
  "error": {"message":"Quota exceeded for org: org_789","type":"rate_limit"}
}
```
sam: Project: proj_453, Org: org_789. Dashboard for proj_453 shows 42k tokens used / 100k limit. Org dashboard shows 98k / 200k (should be fine). Customer sees 429s immediately after a short burst.
maria: Did they hit a per-minute or per-second limit? The 429 looks org-level. Could be rolling-window vs dashboard aggregation mismatch.
olivia: We've seen a bug where short-term token bursts aren't reflected in the dashboard rollups (UI buckets by 1h) but are enforced by a fine-grained sliding window in the rate limiter.
sam: Repro steps supplied by customer:
1) run 10 parallel requests to /v1/generate with ~2k tokens each
2) observe ~3rd-6th request returning 429
3) wait ~2 minutes and requests succeed again
sam: Customer included server logs showing pattern of rapid bursts and immediate 429s with X-RateLimit-Remaining:0 then reset countdown ~90-180s.
quota-bot: Automated quota check: proj_453 usage (24h): 42,120 tokens. org_789 usage (24h): 198,650 tokens. Org hard limit = 200,000 tokens.
alex: So org is close to the cap. The customer says dashboard showed a gap of ~2k tokens available but they still hit 429s. Could it be eventual consistency in the dashboard backing store vs real-time meter?
maria: Likely. Our real-time enforcement reads from the cumulative token stream with 1s resolution; dashboards are summarized with 5m granularity and delayed by up to 90s in the UI. Rapid bursts can push enforcement over the org limit before the dashboard updates.
olivia: Also check whether the customer's requests were routed through multiple projects/org aliases — we had a mapping bug mapping proj_453 traffic to org_789 and an older org_789-legacy counter was double-counting in some windows.
sam: I asked customer for request IDs. They gave three: req_01F..., req_01G..., req_01H... Attached their minimal repro script (they used node):
```
for (let i=0;i<12;i++) fetch('/v1/generate',{method:'POST',headers:{Authorization:'Bearer sk-...'},body:...})
```
```
Response 429 sample: {"error":{"message":"Quota exceeded for org: org_789"}}
```

alex: Next actions:
- maria, can you check enforcement logs for org_789 between 15:20-15:25 UTC for those request ids and confirm if counts spiked above 200k in sliding window? (assigned to @maria)
- olivia, can you grep for the mapping/alias code that aggregates to org_789? possible duplicate counters? (assigned to @olivia)
- sam, reply to customer with explanation and ask for exact timestamps and any proxy/cdn IPs.
maria: I'm seeing an enforcement burst where sliding-window token total peaked at ~201,500 at 15:22:10 UTC due to a few large responses. The dashboard ingestion service shows 198,650 at 15:21:30 then 199,800 at 15:22:00 (90s lag). So enforcement triggered before the dashboard had the updated bucket.
olivia: I also found a rare double-count path for legacy SDKs that report to both streaming and batch meters; not for all requests but matches the IPs in the logs. Patch incoming.
sam: Customer reply: "Thanks. We can throttle to avoid bursts but we rely on dashboard to show available quota. Is there any ETA for better real-time visibility?"
alex: Proposal: add a small real-time "enforcement headroom" indicator in UI showing current enforcement count (1s resolution) + a note about dashboard latency. Mid-term: reduce dashboard lag and add streaming counters.
maria: For this incident, recommended support reply:
- Explain sliding-window enforcement vs dashboard aggregation latency
- Provide exact enforcement timestamps and request IDs
- Suggest immediate mitigation: client-side rate limit (e.g., token bucket) or staggered concurrency
sam: Draft reply to customer:
"We investigated: enforcement uses a fine-grained sliding window and can trigger on short bursts before summary dashboards update. We found your requests caused a transient spike that exceeded your org's sliding-window quota. We're working on improving UI headroom indicators. For now we recommend adding short client-side backoff (retry-after from 429) or limiting concurrency to X requests/sec. Attached logs: [link]."
olivia: I'll open a follow-up ticket for SDK double-counting and include a test to prevent regressions.
quota-bot: Created issue #ENG-5123 for SDK double-counting. Priority: P2.
sam: I'll send the customer the explanation + the three request IDs and close the support ticket once they ack. Marking this thread resolved but keeping notes here for the team. :white_check_mark:
